instruction: Pawn: A pawn moves forward one square, or two from its starting square if both are clear. It captures diagonally. Move the pawn from e2 to e4.
correct_feedback: A pawn can move two squares from its starting position.
incorrect_feedback: That is a legal move, but try the destination described in the lesson.
title: Pawn

instruction: Knight: A knight moves in an L shape and can jump over pieces. Move the knight from b2 to c4.
correct_feedback: The knight moved two ranks and one file.
incorrect_feedback: That is a legal move, but try the destination described in the lesson.
title: Knight

instruction: Bishop: A bishop travels diagonally through empty squares and stays on the same color. Move the bishop from c1 to g5.
correct_feedback: The bishop traveled diagonally along clear squares.
incorrect_feedback: That is a legal move, but try the destination described in the lesson.
title: Bishop

instruction: Rook: A rook travels along ranks or files through empty squares. Move the rook from d2 to d5.
correct_feedback: The rook moved up the d-file.
incorrect_feedback: That is a legal move, but try the destination described in the lesson.
title: Rook

instruction: Queen: A queen combines the rook and bishop moves, traveling along ranks, files or diagonals. Move the queen from d1 to h5.
correct_feedback: The queen traveled diagonally to h5.
incorrect_feedback: That is a legal move, but try the destination described in the lesson.
title: Queen

instruction: King: A king moves one square in any direction, but cannot move into check. Move the king from h1 to g2.
correct_feedback: The king moved one square diagonally.
incorrect_feedback: That is a legal move, but try the destination described in the lesson.
title: King
Pawn capture
instruction: Pawns capture diagonally, not straight ahead. Capture the pawn on d5 with your e4 pawn.
correct_feedback: Correct. The pawn moves diagonally to d5 and removes the black pawn.
incorrect_feedback: Look for the diagonal capture.

title: Knight jumps
instruction: A knight is the only piece that can jump over occupied squares. Move the knight from b1 to c3.
correct_feedback: Correct. The pawns do not block the knight's L-shaped move.
incorrect_feedback: The knight can jump over the pawns to c3.

title: Rook capture
instruction: Rooks capture along open ranks and files. Capture the rook on d5 with the rook on d2.
correct_feedback: Correct. A rook captures the opposing piece on its destination square.
incorrect_feedback: The d-file is open between the rooks.

title: Bishop capture
instruction: Bishops capture along an unobstructed diagonal. Capture the knight on f4 with the bishop on c1.
correct_feedback: Correct. The bishop travels through d2 and e3 to capture on f4.
incorrect_feedback: Follow the diagonal from c1 to f4.

title: Kingside castling
instruction: Castling moves both king and rook. Castle kingside by moving the white king from e1 to g1.
correct_feedback: Correct. The king goes to g1 and the rook moves from h1 to f1.
incorrect_feedback: Move the king two squares toward the rook.

title: Queenside castling
instruction: Black can castle queenside when the route is clear and the king does not cross an attacked square. Move the king from e8 to c8.
correct_feedback: Correct. The black king lands on c8 and the rook moves to d8.
incorrect_feedback: Move the black king two squares toward the queenside rook.

title: En passant
instruction: Black has just moved the d-pawn from d7 to d5. Capture it en passant with the e5 pawn; this chance lasts only one move.
correct_feedback: Correct. The pawn lands on d6 and the black pawn on d5 is removed.
incorrect_feedback: Capture diagonally onto d6, the square the pawn passed.

title: Promote a pawn
instruction: A pawn reaching the far rank must promote. Move a7 to a8 and choose a queen.
correct_feedback: Correct. The pawn becomes a queen and checks the black king.
incorrect_feedback: Move to a8 and choose the queen in the promotion picker.

title: Choose a knight
instruction: Promotion is not limited to a queen. Move the pawn from a7 to a8 and choose a knight.
correct_feedback: Correct. A promotion may produce a queen, rook, bishop or knight.
incorrect_feedback: Move to a8 and choose the knight.

title: Escape a check
instruction: The rook on e8 checks your king. Move the king from e1 to the safe square d1.
correct_feedback: Correct. A king may escape check by moving to an unattacked square.
incorrect_feedback: Move the king off the attacked e-file to d1.

title: Block a check
instruction: The rook checks along the e-file. Block the check by moving the bishop from d2 to e3.
correct_feedback: Correct. A piece placed on e3 interrupts the rook's line to the king.
incorrect_feedback: Place the bishop between the rook and the king.

title: Capture the attacker
instruction: The rook on e2 checks your king and is not defended. Capture it with the king.
correct_feedback: Correct. A king may capture a checking piece if its destination is not attacked.
incorrect_feedback: Capture the undefended rook on e2.

title: Give check
instruction: A check attacks the opposing king. Move the rook from b1 to b8 to check along the eighth rank.
correct_feedback: Correct. The rook attacks the king along the eighth rank.
incorrect_feedback: Put the rook on b8 to attack along the rank.

title: Checkmate in one
instruction: Checkmate means check with no legal escape. Find a queen move that checkmates Black.
correct_feedback: Checkmate. The black king is attacked and has no legal escape.
incorrect_feedback: Look for a queen move that checks and covers the king's escape squares.

title: Knight fork
instruction: A fork attacks two targets at once. Move the knight to check the king and attack the queen on c7.
correct_feedback: Correct. From e6 the knight checks the king on g7 and attacks the queen on c7.
incorrect_feedback: Find an L-shaped jump that attacks both g7 and c7.

title: Pin a knight
instruction: A piece is pinned to its king when moving it would expose the king to check. Move the bishop from f1 to b5.
correct_feedback: Correct. The bishop lines up with the knight on c6 and king on e8; the knight cannot legally move.
incorrect_feedback: Place the bishop on b5, on the same diagonal as the knight and king.

title: Rook skewer
instruction: A skewer attacks a valuable piece with another target behind it. Check the king on a7 with your rook.
correct_feedback: Correct. The king must leave the a-file, exposing the queen behind it.
incorrect_feedback: Move the rook to the a-file to check the king.

title: Win an unprotected rook
instruction: The black rook attacks your queen, but it is unprotected. Capture it with the queen on d2.
correct_feedback: Correct. The queen captures the undefended rook on d8.
incorrect_feedback: Look along the open d-file for the attacking rook.

instruction: White to move: capture the unprotected black queen with the rook.
correct_feedback: Correct! The rook captures the queen.
incorrect_feedback: Look for a rook move that captures the queen.
explanation: The d-file is clear, so the rook can move from d2 to d4 and capture the queen.

instruction: White to move: find a checkmate in one.
correct_feedback: Checkmate! The black king has no legal escape.
incorrect_feedback: That move does not give checkmate. Try another queen move.
explanation: Qf8 is checkmate: the queen checks along the eighth rank, and White controls the black king’s escape squares.

instruction: White to move: promote the pawn to a queen and give check.
correct_feedback: Correct! The new queen checks the king.
incorrect_feedback: Choose the promotion that creates a queen.
explanation: Move the pawn from a7 to a8 and choose a queen. The queen checks the king along the eighth rank.
